newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stadshypotek board not resigning over criticism.
newsitem.headline: Stadshypotek board not resigning over criticism.

text.p: The board of Swedish mortgage lending institution Stadshypotek said it regretted a statement on Monday by Finance Minister Erik Asbrink, in which the minister said he had no confidence in the company's board.
It said in a statement its recommendation to shareholders of a merger with insurer Skandia, announced earlier on Monday, was made with the interest of all shareholders in mind.
Asbrink, whose ministry is tendering for the sale of the state's 34 percent interest in Stadshypotek, criticised the board for allegedly failing to consult the government about its intentions.

"During the period of our discussions with Skandia, and before the decision to recommend the merger to shareholders, we tried to advise the ministry about our plans," the bank said in the statement, which was a copy of a letter sent to Asbrink.
"Representatives of the ministry expressly chose to decline the offer on our part to discuss the possibility of a merger with Skandia or other structural measures."
The board said its proposal about the merger did not prevent the state from carrying out its auction procedure.

"That one large owner plans to dispose of its shares in the company is no reason for a board to delay, at the risk of damaging consequences, measures about the company which the board considers to be for the benefit of the shareholders and the company.

"Members of the board have against this background agreed today not to offer their resignations, well aware of the possibility that the state has to request an extraordinary meeting to deal with the board issue," it said.
